commands.description: Places a prefab, model or mesh where a ray, a Scene view pixel or a point lands, resting on the surface there, as a drop into the Scene view does. One undo step. Exactly one of: ray {origin, direction}; viewport {x, y, width?, height?} (a pixel of the Scene view's image through its camera, as scene.raycast); point [x, y, z] with normal (default [0, 1, 0]), e.g. a scene.raycast hit. A ray or pixel that hits nothing lands on the grid plane y = 0 within 500 m, else on the ray at fallbackDistance (default 10 m; for a pixel the editor camera's distance to its target), unless requireSurface: then it fails. snap (meters) puts the point on that grid along the surface and finds the height there; rotation ([x, y, z] degrees) and scale (uniform) apply over the asset's own. A mesh becomes an entity with a Mesh Renderer, named after it. While the prefab or model loads it waits (at most 30 s), then up to 5 s for what its size needs (after that it places by the size known so far: bounds.pending true). Returns {id (the root), entities (every root), placedOn: surface | grid | inFront | point, hitEntity (null unless surface), point, normal, translation, bounds {min, max, size, center, pending}, snapped}; while playing it changes the running copy only.

commands.description: Asset memory and streaming: resident bytes and budget per pool (cpu, gpuTextures, gpuBuffers; null budget = unlimited), load counts, the streaming queue (queued loads per priority, loads and bytes in flight), finalization (GPU bytes uploaded and main-thread milliseconds, and of those the milliseconds of the upload steps, last frame and maximum of recent frames, with their budgets and the staging budget), evictions (and how many resident assets eviction looked at), cancellations, staging releases and dependency prefetches (prefetch: loads of what assets reference started when their reads completed, and those dropped on arrival for lack of room in the budgets) and mip streaming (mipStreaming: loads of only a texture's header and smallest levels, reads of further levels queued and completed, levels raised and dropped (and of those dropped, the levels a budget took: its pressure, or room for detail a view needs more), bytes read for them in all and in the last frame, textures below the level their views need, and textures reading or changing levels now), and importMemoryMB (the imports' memory estimates: admitted, budget, queued). With assets: true it also lists the assets that are resident, loading, failed or pinned, with their memory, state, last use and pins; streaming textures add residentMip (the finest mip level resident, 0 the full resolution), wantedMip (the finest level their views need), mipCount and residentBytes (what the resident levels hold). geometryPool is the renderer's pool of every mesh's GPU geometry (usedMB, capacityMB, allocations, fragmentation of its free space, moves and growths so far; null without a GPU): meshes count their ranges of it as gpuBuffers.

commands.description: What people, agents and scripts did in this editor: the activity journal of every command run (the latest 2,000, within 8 MB), oldest first after since. Each entry: {id, parent (the command that ran it), time (milliseconds since 1970-01-01 UTC), source (UI, Automation, CommandScript or Internal), client (an automation client's name), command, summary (in a few words, as the Activity panel lists it: the undo step with the entities' names, the error's first line, the warning, or done), mutating, playing (ran while the scene played), runningCopy (changed the playing scene's running copy, which play.stop discarded), parameters (parametersTruncated when too large to keep), status (Pending, Succeeded, Failed), result (a summary) or error {kind, message}, warning, durationMs, frames (of a command that took several), entities (that its undo step touched, at most 256) and entityCount, undoStep}. Page with since = the returned latest while more is true, or with newest: true (the latest first) with before = the returned oldest; editor.activity.export turns entries into a command script.

before.description: Return entries with an id below this (default: none)

command.description: Only entries of this command, or of a group with a prefix ending in '.' ("entity.")

commands.description: Writes the successful edits after an entry of the activity journal (editor.activity; since 0: from the session's start) as a command script for StrataEditor --commands, to repeat a session on a copy of the project as it was at that point, e.g. as a regression script: commands of kind Edit (editor.commands), also those run while playing that outlast play mode (materials, assets, scene.save), but not edits of a playing scene's running copy (play.stop discarded them: skippedWhilePlaying). Entities and assets the session created get new IDs every run, so the script binds them where a result gave them ("bind": {"e12.id": "/id"}) and refers to them where they are used ({"$ref": "e12.id"}); queries of the project's content whose results later edits took IDs from are part of the script too (IDs from results that follow the editor's session, such as selection.get and editor.status, stay as they are). Returns {path, steps, edits, lookups, bindings, skippedWhilePlaying, editsOutsideCommands, unrepeatableEdits, warning?, since, latest}: changes made outside commands (inspector fields, gizmo drags, the material editor record their undo steps directly) and the undo steps of commands a script does not repeat (scene.recover) cannot be in the script, and a warning says so when there were any. Fails when the journal no longer holds every entry after since (it keeps at most 2,000 commands and 8 MB of them: export from a later entry then), or when the parameters of a command the script needs were too large to keep.

At most 1,000 steps; commands that can take frames (loads, builds, imports, captures, saves, play.step, input with wait: MayDefer) and editor.batch itself are refused before anything runs. atomic (default true): a failed step undoes the steps before it, records no undo step and fails the batch naming the step's index; atomic false runs every step and keeps what succeeded. commands.description: Where the editor's frames go: statistics of the latest frames the frame profiler recorded (at most 600). Returns frames (how many were summarized), frame (the CPU time of a frame without the waits for the GPU and the display, like the status bar's frame time), framesPerSecond, interval (the time from one frame's start to the next: what a frame-rate cap, vsync or idle throttling sets), stages (per stage of the main thread: Input, Assets.Update, Assets.Finalize, Scene.Load (swapping in a scene that finished loading, creating sub-scenes' entities), Scene.UI (the game UI's input), Scene.Scripts, Scene.Animation, Scene.Physics, Scene.Audio, Scene.Transforms, Render.Extract, Render.Submit, Render.UI (the game UI pass), Editor.UI and Present, plus stages modules registered; each its self time, nested stages excluded, with inFrameTime false for Present: presenting after the frame, and the wait for the display's image at the back buffer's first use inside it; neither counts as the frame's work), stageSum (the stages inside the frame time added up per frame), untimed (the rest of each frame, work no stage accounts for) and jobs (worker, I/O and background threads (imports, exports), how busy they were in percent, running and queued jobs now). gpu is the GPU's side of the same frames, known 2-3 frames late: frames (with GPU times), latencyFrames, busy (the GPU stages added up per frame), stages (per GPU stage: GPU.Uploads, GPU.Setup, GPU.Aerial (the atmosphere's aerial perspective), GPU.Cull, GPU.Shadows, GPU.Prepass, GPU.ScreenShadows (the sun's shadow mask), GPU.AO, GPU.RadianceCascades (global illumination: voxels), GPU.Reflections (reflection probes' conversions, screen-space reflections), GPU.Opaque (with the sky), GPU.Transparent, GPU.TAA (motion vectors' history and temporal anti-aliasing), GPU.MotionBlur, GPU.DepthOfField, GPU.Post, GPU.Overlays, GPU.UI (the game UI), GPU.ImGui) and boundBy: gpu when the GPU's median busy time takes at least 90% of the median frame interval and exceeds the CPU's frame time, cpu when the CPU's does, capped when neither does (vsync or a frame-rate cap sets the pace), unknown without GPU times. renderStats is the viewport's latest frame (null while it renders none): quality (the Graphics Quality it drew with, as project.settings shows Renderer.Quality), shadowMapSize (the sun's cascades' texels), cascades (each sun cascade's slice near and far in meters of view distance and texelSize in meters: stable cascades, which depend on the view alone), localShadowTileSizes (the tiles of the first 64 shadowed point and spot lights by rank), localShadowTileSizeCounts (how many have tiles of each size, by size in texels), gpuDriven (the frame took the GPU-driven path: its counts are the GPU's, of a frame 2-3 frames older, once gpuCounts is true; transparent surfaces are the CPU's), gpuCulled (the GPU culled the scene's mesh renderers and built their draws; false in a scene without mesh renderers, whose frames record no culling and take their requests from the CPU), feedbackRequests (its asset requests came from the GPU's visibility feedback of an earlier frame, not from the CPU walking the view), drawCommands (draw calls the CPU recorded), draws (instanced draws of the view), opaqueDraws, shadowDraws, instances, shadowCasters, triangles, visibleProxies, occludedProxies (in the frustum but hidden behind what the view draws: left out on the GPU-driven path), occludedCasters (shadow casters hidden from the light behind other casters, per cascade: left out of those cascades on the GPU-driven path), cachedCascades (shadow cascades kept from the previous frame: nothing reaching them changed), localShadowRequested (shadowed point, spot and rect lights in view, which ask for a shadow), localShadowLights (those given one: Graphics Quality's MaxShadowedLocalLights and the atlas decide), localShadowFading (those fading the shadow they lost out), localShadowViewsDrawn (their shadow views drawn: none while nothing reaching them changed), localShadowViewsPending, localShadowCasters, reflectionProbes (reflection probes the view shaded with), reflectionProbesPending (in view, their capture still loading or waiting to be converted), culledProxies, sizeCulledProxies (in view but below a pixel), instancesPerLod, lights, areaLights (of lights, the rect lights), areaLightShading (the forward passes used the shaders that shade rect lights, a little costlier: the scene has a rect light, lit or not, in view or not), areaShadowMasks (the shadowed rect lights whose shadows opaque surfaces took from screen-space masks, at most 4), areaShadowTiles (the atlas tiles the shadowed rect lights hold, six each), droppedLights, materials, pendingAssets, extractMs, sortMs, proxyUpdates, instanceBytesUploaded, deferredInstanceBytes (new mesh renderers waiting for their upload to the GPU), geometryPool (the meshes' GPU geometry: usedMB, capacityMB, allocations, fragmentation, moves, growths), sceneMirrorMB (the GPU memory of the scenes' GPU copies: a playing scene's doubles its scene's), exposure (what automatic exposure metered, frames late: ev100, EV100 = log2 of the metered luminance in nits + 3; keyStops, the exposure key's darkening, 0 or below; cardEv100, the EV100 of a gray card in the directional light's light, null without one; exposure is null with manual exposure), motionBlur (samples, tileSize in pixels; null on frames that did not blur), depthOfField (focusDistance in meters, focalLength in millimeters, fNumber, infinityBlurPixels: the blur's diameter of a point infinitely far; null without a lens), colorLookup (whether the Post Process's color lookup was applied; false while it loads), lensFlare (sunInFront: whether the directional light's disk was in front of the camera for the starburst; null when lens flares did not run), globalIllumination (ran, pending: its voxels incomplete, settled: nothing left to voxelize; null without GI), gpuMs (per GPU stage of the frame gpuStatsFrame names). gameRenderStats is the same for the Game view's latest frame (null while it is hidden or closed); both views' GPU work adds up in gpu's stages. commands.description: Overview of the editor; start here to orient yourself. entities.description: Entities to duplicate (instead of entity); those below another listed one are copied with it (entity IDs)

commands.name: entity.find

box.description: A world-space box {min: [x, y, z], max: [x, y, z]}

commands.description: An entity's name, parent, children and all component values, and inactive: {Component: {Property: reason}} for properties that have no effect in their component's state (e.g. a bloom threshold while Bloom is off; left out when none). With world: true also where it is in the world, decomposed from its world transform: world: {position, rotation: {euler (degrees, as the Inspector shows them), quaternion [x, y, z, w]}, scale}, and what it and its descendants take up: bounds: {min, max, size, center, pending} (what renders, skinned meshes in their pose; else physical shapes; else boxes around the entities; pending: a mesh still loading stood in as a box: ask again).
commands.name: entity.get

world.description: Add world (the world transform) and bounds (default false)

Top-level entities whose names their new siblings have get a number ('Crate' -> 'Crate (1)'). Returns the IDs of the pasted top-level entities and warnings about data this build cannot read.
commands.name: entity.paste

index.description: Position of the first pasted entity among the parent's children (default: last)

parent.description: Parent of the pasted entities; null or omitted for the top level (entity ID or null)

commands.description: Renames an entity (undoable; while playing it changes the running copy only). Returns {entity, name}.

commands.name: entity.setParent

entities.description: Entities to move (instead of entity), in the order they end up in; those below another listed one move with it (entity IDs)

keepWorldTransform.description: Keep the world-space placement of entities that change parent (default true)

parent.description: New parent; null or omitted for the top level (entity ID or null)

commands.description: Deletes the players' graphics options of the project's game: the file <project>/.strata/Saves/GraphicsOptions.json that a game's options menu wrote with Graphics::Save while the game played here, and that every play session starts with, so that the project's Graphics Quality (the settings section Renderer.Quality, project.setSettings) applies in play again (while the file sets the preset, changes of the project's preset do not show in play; the Graphics Quality page says so). commands.description: Holds an input action of the running game (play mode) directly, whatever its bindings, as if a player used its controls: scripts see it through Input::IsActionDown/IsActionPressed/IsActionReleased and GetActionValue, and the game UI navigates with the UI map's (UI/Submit, UI/Cancel, UI/Up...). tap (default) holds it for 'steps' fixed steps of the game (or 'seconds' of game time), press until a release (or input.releaseAll, play.stop), release ends its hold. An action has one hold: a new tap or press replaces the one before (ending it, interrupted when it was a tap) without letting the action go. value: an Axis' [x, 0] (default [1, 0]), a Vector2's [x, y] (required, length at most 1); a Button takes none. The game still reads it as up while its map is disabled or a binding capture listens. Keys given with input.key reach actions through their bindings instead. Answers once the game has seen the input (a tap: its release), or at once with wait false (the default while paused). Returns action (its qualified name), kind, mode, value, seen, and what is still held.

action.description: The action: "<Map>/<Action>", or its bare name when no other map has an action so named (input.state lists them)

frames.description: Same as steps (an older name: they used to count frames)

commands.description: Simulated input in the running game: the keys, mouse buttons and gamepad buttons the input.* commands hold, the gamepad axes they hold with their values, the input actions input.action holds with theirs (simulatedActions), the gamepads simulated input connected (gamepads), the pointer position the game sees (null until input.mouseMove), whether the game is paused so input waits for its next frame (paused), whether input is waiting for that frame (queued), every hold with the fixed steps it covers (holds: [{type, name, firstStep, lastStep (null until released)}]), the game's fixed steps so far (fixedSteps) and whether an input.sequence runs (sequenceRunning). Device input (a person at the keyboard) is not included in those. The game's input actions as it reads them now (actions: [{action, map, kind, down, value}], device input included), the maps' enables (maps: [{map, enabled}]), the players' bindings that replace the project's (playerBindings: {action: [bindings]}, see inputActions.resetPlayerBindings) and whether a binding capture listens (capture: every action reads as up meanwhile).
commands.name: input.state

commands.description: Types text into the running game (play mode), as a keyboard with its layout and input method would: scripts read it with Input::GetTypedText in the next game frame (UTF-8, at most 1,024 bytes a frame; malformed UTF-8 arrives as U+FFFD). Answers once the game has seen it, or at once with wait false (the default while paused).
commands.name: input.type

text.description: The text to type (UTF-8, 1 to 1,024 bytes)

wait.description: Answer once the game has seen the input (default: true while the game runs; false while it is paused without a pending step, because the input then waits for play.step or play.pause false and the command would wait with it)

commands.description: Deletes the players' bindings of the project's game: the file <project>/.strata/Saves/InputBindings.json that a rebinding menu wrote with Input::SaveBindings while the game played here, and that every play session starts with, so that the project's bindings apply again (while the file rebinds an action, inputActions.setAction's bindings do not reach play mode for it; the Input Actions page marks those actions). While playing, the running game also gets the project's bindings back from its next frame. Not undoable, like the game's saves. Returns reset: the actions whose players' bindings were dropped.
commands.name: inputActions.resetPlayerBindings

commands.description: Adds, changes, moves or removes an action of the project's input actions (the project settings section Input.Actions). The action is named "<Map>/<Action>" or by a bare name no other map has; an unknown one is added to its map (the map in its name, or map; inputActions.setMap adds maps) with kind (Button, the default; Axis: one value from -1 to 1; Vector2: two, +Y up), deadZone (Axis and Vector2: 0 to 0.9, default 0.15) and bindings. An existing one takes the changes given: rename, kind (its bindings must fit the new kind, or give new ones), deadZone, bindings (replaces the whole list, at most 8), map (moves it), or remove: true. Bindings are texts: Key/<key>, Mouse/<button>, Gamepad/<button>; Gamepad/<axis>, Gamepad/<axis>+ or -, Gamepad/LeftStick or RightStick; 1D:<negative>,<positive> and 2D:<up>,<down>,<left>,<right> of button-like controls. The UI map's Submit, Cancel, Up, Down, Left and Right (the game UI's navigation) take new bindings but cannot be renamed, moved, removed or made another kind. One undo step that leaves the scene saved; writes the project file in the background. Allowed while playing: the running game reads the change in its next frame. Returns action ({name, kind, deadZone, bindings, reserved}) and created, or removed.
commands.name: inputActions.setAction

action.description: The action: "<Map>/<Action>", or a bare name no other map has

bindings.description: Key/<key>, Mouse/<button>, Gamepad/<button> (InputNames' names, any gamepad); Gamepad/<axis> (whole axis), Gamepad/<axis>+ or - (half axis; triggers only +), Gamepad/LeftStick or RightStick; 1D:<negative>,<positive> and 2D:<up>,<down>,<left>,<right> of keys, mouse and gamepad buttons and half axes

deadZone.description: Axis and Vector2: values within it read 0, the rest is rescaled to reach 1 (round for vectors)

map.description: The map to add the action to, or to move it to

remove.description: Removes the action (no other change may be given)

rename.description: A new name for the action (unique in its map, ignoring case)

commands.description: Adds, changes or removes a map of the project's input actions (the project settings section Input.Actions; project.settings shows them all): a map unknown so far is added (enabled says whether its actions work when the game starts, default true); an existing one is renamed (rename) or enabled at start or not (enabled), or removed with its actions (remove: true). The map UI is reserved for the game UI's navigation and cannot be renamed or removed. Names are 1 to 64 letters, digits, spaces, '_', '-' and '.', unique ignoring case; at most 32 maps. One undo step that leaves the scene saved; writes the project file in the background. Allowed while playing: the running game reads the change in its next frame. Returns map ({name, enabled, reserved, actions}) and created, or removed.
commands.name: inputActions.setMap

enabled.description: Whether the map's actions work when the game starts (scripts enable and disable maps while it runs)

remove.description: Removes the map and its actions (no other change may be given)

rename.description: A new name for the map

commands.description: Lights the scene with a sun and sky preset: Clear (the physical atmosphere, a 120,000 lux sun 40 degrees up: sunny, deep blue shadows), Hazy (thicker air, a paler sky and softer contrast), Overcast (an even gray sky of about 7,700 lux and a faint, very soft sun) or GoldenHour (the sun 6 degrees up, warm light and long shadows). Writes the sky light's source and settings and the directional light's rotation, intensity, color and shadow softness; keeps the light's azimuth unless sunAzimuth is given. A real sun clips to white under the active Post Process's manual exposure, so that turns automatic (Exposure compensation 0), and its AutoExposureMaxEV is raised to 16 when below 15. Creates 'Sky' or 'Sun' when the scene has none. One undo step; while playing it changes the running copy (warning). Returns {preset, changed, sky, light, createdSky, createdLight, sunDirection (toward the sun), sunIntensity (lux above the air), groundIlluminance (lux on a surface facing the sun at the ground), postProcess (the entity whose exposure was changed, or null), autoExposureTurnedOn (its manual exposure became automatic)}.
commands.name: lighting.applySkyPreset

light.description: The entity with the DirectionalLight to write; default: the brightest active one, or a new 'Sun' (entity ID)

sky.description: The entity with the SkyLight to write; default: the scene's first active sky light, or a new 'Sky' (entity ID)

sunAzimuth.description: Degrees from +X toward +Z of the direction toward the sun (default: the light's own, or 20)

sunElevation.description: Degrees above the horizon (default: the preset's)

commands.description: Bakes reflection probes: renders what each one sees from where it stands now (the edited scene as it is: lights, sky, fog and the probes' current captures, its own included, so every further bake adds a bounce) into a new equirectangular HDR texture, Assets/Lighting/<scene>/<probe id>.hdr (' (n)' added when the name is taken), and sets the probe's Capture to it. The capture an earlier bake made for the probe goes to the trash once nothing else uses it (the open scene as it is in memory, even while its saved file still names it); any other texture Capture named stays. One undo step for the files and the captures. Answers once the textures are imported (a few frames; the editor keeps running). Needs a GPU; refused while playing (it renders and writes from the edited scene). Returns {directory, probes: [{entity, name, capture, path, complete (false when something it sees was still loading after two minutes), previous (the capture before, or null), trashed}]}.
commands.name: lighting.bakeProbes

entities.description: Probes to bake (entities with a ReflectionProbe component); default: every active probe of the scene (entity IDs)

commands.description: Makes the scene's directional light the sun of its sky's environment map: finds the map's sun in its source file (the brightest texel and the texels around it at least 4 times as bright as the sky there, at most 3 degrees across) and writes the light's rotation (pointing away from the sun as the sky shows it, the sky's Rotation applied), Color (the sun's color, its largest channel 1) and Intensity (the sun's illuminance in lux, times the sky's Intensity). The light is `light`, else the brightest active directional light, else a new entity 'Sun'. One undo step (none when the light already is that sun). Run asset.setImportSettings {"RemoveSun": true} on the map afterwards so the sun does not light the scene twice (the Sky section's Extract Sun does both). Reads the file in the background and answers in a few frames; refused while playing. Returns {light, created, changed, map, direction (toward the sun), color, intensity, illuminance (the sun's luminance per unit of the sky's Intensity), angularDiameter (degrees), texels, clipped (the file clipped the sun: its light is a lower bound, and warning says so)}.
commands.name: lighting.extractSun

light.description: The entity with a DirectionalLight to write; default: the brightest active one, or a new 'Sun' (entity ID)

sky.description: The entity with the SkyLight whose environment map holds the sun; default: the scene's first active sky light (entity ID)

commands.description: Makes an emissive panel a real light: adds a child Rect Light on the panel's emitting face with the panel's luminance and size (Units Nits), and tags the panel Light Surface so its emission is not counted twice (screen-space reflections, probe captures and the light's own shadows leave it out). Use it on any thin emissive mesh (ceiling panels, signs, screens); the panel keeps its look. `side` auto takes the thinnest axis of the mesh's bounds times the panel's world scale when it is under half of the next, and of its two faces the lower one when that axis is within 45 degrees of vertical (a ceiling panel); pass side for wall panels. Waits while the mesh or material loads; fails, changing nothing, on an entity without a mesh, a material that emits nothing, a face that already has a Rect Light child, or while playing. One undo step removes the light and the tag. Returns {light, panel, side, size (meters in the world), luminance (nits), color, lumens (pi x luminance x area, twice for two-sided), tagged (the tag was added)}.
commands.name: lighting.makeAreaLight

castShadows.description: The light casts soft shadows (default true)

entity.description: The emissive panel: an entity with a MeshRenderer (entity ID)

offset.description: Meters in front of the face, along its outward normal (default 0.001): keeps the light off the panel's own surface

side.description: Which face of the mesh's local axes emits; default auto

twoSided.description: The light emits from both faces (default false)

commands.description: Log messages (engine, editor and scripts), oldest first after a sequence number, or with newest: true the latest first. Reading from level Error or below without a logger marks the errors read for editor.status (errors.unread).
commands.name: log.read

before.description: Only messages with a sequence number below this (default: none)

logger.description: Only messages of this logger (exact name, e.g. Strata, App, Script)

newest.description: Newest first: the latest messages (default false: oldest first)

commands.description: Creates a material asset (.stmat) from the default material with the given property values. Returns {asset, warnings}: textures whose import usage does not fit their slot (see material.get).
commands.name: material.create

path.description: Path relative to the asset directory, e.g. "Materials/Red.stmat"

properties.description: Property values, e.g. {"BaseColor": [1, 0, 0, 1], "Roughness": 0.3, "BaseColorMap": "Textures/Brick.png"}; texture maps take a texture by path or handle, null clears them. Properties: BaseColor, Metallic, Roughness, EmissiveColor, EmissiveIntensity, NormalScale, OcclusionStrength, AlphaMode, AlphaCutoff, DoubleSided, Unlit, UVTiling, UVOffset, BaseColorMap, MetallicRoughnessMap, NormalMap, OcclusionMap, EmissiveMap, Clearcoat, ClearcoatRoughness, ClearcoatMap, ClearcoatRoughnessMap, ClearcoatNormalMap, Transmission, TransmissionMap, IOR, Thickness, AttenuationColor, AttenuationDistance (material.get describes their types)

commands.description: A material asset's property values, and every material property with its type, range or options: what material.create and material.set accept. "saved" is false while values previewed with material.set {save: false} are not saved. "warnings" lists texture maps whose import usage does not fit their slot (a Color texture as the normal map, color in Metal/Rough or Occlusion, a normal map or data as color): [{property, texture, usage, expected, message, fix: {command, parameters}}]; run fix (asset.setImportSettings) to import the texture as the slot reads it.
commands.name: material.get

material.description: Material: handle, path or Builtin/DefaultMaterial (asset handle, or path relative to the asset directory)

commands.description: Changes property values of a material asset of the project; entities using it show the change in the same frame. By default it saves the material (one undo step, edit.undo restores the file and the loaded values); save: false only previews the values in the loaded material (no file is written, no undo step), e.g. while a value is dragged, until a saving material.set (which saves them too), an undo or a reload replaces them. Returns the material's values and warnings (texture maps whose import usage does not fit their slot, with the command that fixes each: see material.get).
commands.name: material.set

material.description: Material (asset handle, or path relative to the asset directory)

properties.description: Property values to change, e.g. {"BaseColor": [1, 0, 0, 1]}. Properties: BaseColor, Metallic, Roughness, EmissiveColor, EmissiveIntensity, NormalScale, OcclusionStrength, AlphaMode, AlphaCutoff, DoubleSided, Unlit, UVTiling, UVOffset, BaseColorMap, MetallicRoughnessMap, NormalMap, OcclusionMap, EmissiveMap, Clearcoat, ClearcoatRoughness, ClearcoatMap, ClearcoatRoughnessMap, ClearcoatNormalMap, Transmission, TransmissionMap, IOR, Thickness, AttenuationColor, AttenuationDistance (material.get describes their types)

save.description: Save the material and record an undo step (default true); false previews the values without saving

commands.description: Turns box3d's counters (islands; contacts total, awake and recycled) on or off for every step of the running game (play or simulate), where physics.stats {detail: true} reads them once: while on, physics.stats reports them after each step (contacts.detailed is true from the next step on) and the Streaming panel's Physics section shows the share of the awake contacts box3d recycled. box3d counts them together with its memory, about 0.1 ms a step at 70,000 bodies, so they are off by default. Holds for the running scene until play stops; a scene the game switches to starts without them. Fails while editing and when the running scene has no physics. Returns enabled.
commands.name: physics.setDetailedStats

enabled.description: Read box3d's counters after every step (true) or no longer (false)

commands.description: The physics of the running game (play or simulate): bodies in the simulation (total, static, dynamic, kinematic, awake, character controllers; parked: static bodies out of it that collide with nothing until box3d drops them a second later) and the bodies in use, the world's room (maxBodies: as it grew; growthLimit: the most it may hold; maxContactConstraints) and the memory it takes (reservedMB), bodies waiting at the growth limit (waitingForSlot: below it no body waits) and waiting for other reasons (meshes loading, degenerate transforms), the bodies built and destroyed and the milliseconds spent on it in the last frame, the slices a switched-to scene's bodies were built in while it loaded (preparedSlices; 0 when they were built as the scene started), the world's growths past its room (count, the last one's milliseconds and room), what the world needed beyond the room it was created with (demand: the scene's next world reserves it), the last step's milliseconds, the steps run, the steps held while mesh colliders wait for their meshes, and whether the last step was held. What the last step did: step (ms; libraryMs, box3d's own part; strataMs, Strata's, in parts apply, sync, characters, checkedPairs, events, writeBack, pairs and instruments; library: box3d's stages pairs, collide, solve and sensors, which add up to libraryMs, and the parts of solve constraints, transforms, refit, continuous and islands, besides splitIslands; workers: box3d's; totalMs and totalLibraryMs since the running scene's physics world was created: difference two reads of one world, as a scene switch or a restart makes a new world and starts them from 0), sleep (awake, sleeping and moving bodies, islands), contacts (total, awake and recycled: box3d's reuse of resting contacts without new collision work, and recycledShare of the awake ones; tracked: touching entity pairs someone listens to; capacity; peak: the most contacts box3d held; roomGrowths: box3d steps whose new contacts grew its contact storage while playing, counted after the step that follows; lastGrowthStepMs: the library time of the last of them) and settling (maxSpeed of the moving bodies in m/s; settling: those faster than the sleep threshold; restingJitterMm: how far the others still move in a step). box3d's counters (islands; contacts total, awake and recycled) are read every step only while detailed statistics are on (physics.setDetailedStats, the perf lab, a game run with a perf log; contacts.detailed: the last step read them); otherwise detail: true reads them once for this answer (box3d's last step) and changes nothing, and without it they are null. settings: the tuning the world runs with (contactRecycleDistance in meters, sleepThreshold in m/s, contactHertz; effectiveContactHertz: what box3d uses, at most an eighth of its substep rate, 30 at 60 fixed steps per second; contactDampingRatio, contactPushSpeed) and its source (project: the project's Physics.Simulation section, which project.setSettings changes while the game runs, from its next fixed step; defaults); null without a world. interpolation: what is drawn between the last two fixed steps (enabled, stepAlpha: how far between their poses this frame draws; entities; blended: moved by the steps, composed: carried by what moved, exact: drawn where it is). {running: false} while editing; simulating is false while a running scene has no physics components.
commands.name: physics.stats

detail.description: Read box3d's island and contact counters for this answer when they are not read every step (default false)

commands.description: Pauses or resumes the running scene.
commands.name: play.pause

commands.description: Runs a copy of the scene with physics only (no scripts or audio).
commands.name: play.simulate

commands.description: Runs a copy of the scene with scripts, physics and audio. Changes made while playing are discarded by play.stop. When the project's scripts need building first (their sources changed since the module was built, or scenes use scripts that are not built or loaded), it builds them, then plays the new code: the answer comes once the build finished (a failed build fails play.start with its first errors; script.status lists every diagnostic). A build already running is waited for. While a scene is being opened (scene.open) it fails at once, building nothing. paused: true starts the game paused before its first fixed step (fixedSteps 0, also after a build), so play.step, input.sequence and viewport.capture {live, atFixedStep} see it from its first step. Returns the play state and, when it built, built: {build, seconds, reason}.
commands.name: play.start

build.description: Build the scripts first when they need it (default true); false plays what is loaded

paused.description: Start paused before the first fixed step (default false)

commands.description: Whether the scene is being edited, played or simulated, whether it is paused, the steps play.step still runs (pendingSteps), the fixed steps run since play started (fixedSteps), and what runs (running, null in edit mode): {scene (the scene asset the game switched to, null while the edited scene's copy runs), name, path, entityCount, subScenes: [{id, scene, name, state, entities}] (a world's cells are left out: world sums them up), world: {world, cellsWanted, cellsLoading, cellsLoaded, cellsUnloading, cellsFailed} while a world streams, else null, physics: {bodies (body slots in use), awake, stepMs (the last physics step)} or null without a physics world (physics.stats has more), interpolation: {enabled: drawn between fixed steps (the project's Scene.Timing Interpolation in games, Play and Simulate outside scripted runs), stepAlpha: how far between the last two steps' poses this frame draws, entities: how many are drawn between them}, switching: {scene, progress} while a scene the game asked for loads, else null}.
commands.name: play.state

commands.description: While paused, runs fixed steps of the game, one per frame (frames run unthrottled meanwhile, so 600 steps take the frames' work, not ten seconds), and answers once its last step ran: {state, paused, stepsRun, frameIndex, time, fixedSteps (run since play started)}. Results are exact: the same steps give the same state whatever the frame rate. A play.step while another waits adds its steps after them and answers when its own last step ran. If the game is resumed (play.pause {paused: false} drops steps not run yet), stopped, crashes or quits first, it fails with stepsRun so far. wait: false answers at once with pendingSteps (the steps run over the next frames).
commands.name: play.step

frames.description: Same as steps (an older name: each step runs in a frame of its own)

wait.description: Answer once the steps ran (default true); false answers at once

commands.description: Stops play or simulate mode and returns to the edited scene.
commands.name: play.stop

commands.description: Writes a prefab instance (the instance the entity belongs to: its root's subtree, also entities added to it) back into its prefab, keeping the prefab's own root transform and name; with component (and property), only that override of the entity (prefab.status lists them). Every other instance takes the new values except where it overrides them; entities added to the instance are linked. One undo step for the file and the scene (edit.undo restores both). Edit mode only; imported models cannot be changed (prefab.unpack them, or prefab.create a prefab). An outdated instance (prefab.status: made from an older version, it missed the prefab's later changes) is refused unless force: true, since it would write its older values over them. Returns {prefab, path, root, updatedInstances, linked}.
commands.name: prefab.apply

component.description: Apply only this component of the entity (added, removed or changed)

entity.description: An entity of the instance (its root or below); with component, the entity whose override is applied (entity ID)

force.description: Apply an outdated instance anyway, writing its values over the prefab's later changes (default false)

property.description: With component: apply only this property (scripts: <Class> or <Class>.<Field>)

commands.description: Saves entities and their descendants as a new prefab asset (.stprefab). With link (the default) they become an instance of it, linked as prefab.instantiate's instances are (prefab.apply, prefab.revert, prefab.status); one undo step for the file and the link (edit.undo moves the file to the trash and unlinks them). Links of another prefab they had are replaced. Returns {asset, path, linked}.
commands.name: prefab.create

entities.description: Root entities of the prefab (entity IDs)

link.description: Make the entities an instance of the new prefab (default true; not while playing; refused while a scene is being opened)

path.description: Path relative to the asset directory

commands.description: Instantiates a prefab or imported model, optionally under a parent and with component values on its root (undoable; while playing it changes the running copy only). An instance whose name a sibling has gets a number ('Crate' -> 'Crate (1)'). Returns {id (the first root), entities (every root)}; the instance stays linked to the prefab (prefab.status, prefab.apply, prefab.revert). With instances: [{parent?, components?}] (instead of parent and components) it makes many in one undo step, at most 100,000, and returns {instances: [{id, entities}]} in their order; instances that give only a Transform are made together, the fastest way.
commands.name: prefab.instantiate

components.description: Component values applied to the instance's root, e.g. {"Transform": {"Translation": [2, 0, 0]}}

instances.description: Many instances in one step: [{parent?, components?}], each like the parameters of one

parent.description: Parent; null or omitted for the top level (entity ID or null)

prefab.description: Prefab or model (asset handle, or path relative to the asset directory)

commands.description: Gives a prefab instance (the instance the entity belongs to) its prefab's values again: entities keep their IDs (matched by the prefab's entity ids), entities the prefab lacks go, entities the instance lacks are made, and the root keeps its parent, place, transform and name. With component (and property), only that component (or property) of the entity reverts: a component the prefab lacks goes, one the entity lacks comes back. One undo step (while playing it changes the running copy only). Returns {root, prefab, created}.
commands.name: prefab.revert

component.description: Revert only this component of the entity

entity.description: An entity of the instance (its root or below); with component, the entity whose override is reverted (entity ID)

property.description: With component: revert only this property (scripts: <Class> or <Class>.<Field>)

commands.description: Selects the root of the prefab instance the entity belongs to, or with asset: true shows its prefab in the asset inspector (the Content Browser reveals it). Returns {root, prefab}.
commands.name: prefab.select

asset.description: Inspect the prefab asset instead of selecting the root (default false)

entity.description: An entity of the instance (its root or below) (entity ID)

commands.description: Whether an entity belongs to a prefab instance and how the instance differs from its prefab as stored now (the root's transform and name are the instance's own and never count): {linked, root, prefab, path, modified, outdated, changed: [entity ids whose values differ], added: [entities the prefab lacks], removed: [ids of prefab entities the instance lacks], overrides: [{entity (the scene's; null for an entity the instance removed), prefabEntity, component, property (script fields: <Class>.<Field>), kind: Property | AddedComponent | RemovedComponent | RemovedEntity}]}; {linked: false} for entities of no instance. Prefab changes reach every instance except where it overrides them. outdated: the instance was made from an older version of the prefab and did not take its later changes (it was modified meanwhile), so prefab.apply would write its older values back.
commands.name: prefab.status

entity.description: An entity of the active scene (entity ID)

commands.description: Ends the link between a prefab instance (the instance the entity belongs to) and its prefab: its entities stay as they are, as plain entities. One undo step (while playing it changes the running copy only). Returns {root, entities (how many were unlinked)}.
commands.name: prefab.unpack

entity.description: An entity of the instance (its root or below) (entity ID)

commands.description: The person's preferences, which hold for every project and are kept in their own preferences file (not the project's): every preference section the editor and the engine's modules register (sections: id, title, category, description, version, schema: the JSON Schema of its value, value: what applies, isDefault: whether it is left at its default, problem: why a stored value is refused, null when none), in registration order; unclaimed lists sections the file stores that this editor does not know (kept as stored); file (null while the preferences are kept in memory only), fileState (written, writing or unwritten: its last write failed, preferences.save) and fileError; readOnly says why the file is left as it is (a later editor wrote it: this editor uses the defaults and changes nothing), null otherwise. section narrows sections to one. The value replaces the section's whole value and is checked by the section first: an invalid one changes nothing and fails naming what is wrong; it also fails while the file is left as it is (preferences.get's readOnly). commands.description: Creates a project in a directory and opens it. With template "basic3d" it starts with a saved, lit start scene (Scenes/Main.stscene: Main Camera, Sun, Sky, Ground, Post Process); the default "empty" has no scene (see project.templates). Fails while the edited scene has unsaved changes, or the open project's file unwritten settings (its last write failed: project.save), unless force is true (save first), before anything is created; waits for saves in flight (scene.save, the project file) first. Returns projectFile, template, startScene, discardedChanges and discardedSettings (whether unsaved scene changes or unwritten settings were discarded).
commands.name: project.create

force.description: Go on although the edited scene has unsaved changes, discarding them (default false: the command fails instead). Discarded changes are kept as recovery data of the project (scene.recoveryStatus), and the person at the editor is told who discarded them

commands.description: Exports the project as a playable game (runtime executable, asset pack, script module, manifest) into a directory outside the project, in the background: the editor keeps running, and the command answers when the export finished (it fails at once when it cannot start, and fails naming the document when a scene, prefab or material saved meanwhile references what the export did not plan for: export again, or when the save of the scene in flight that it started during fails). The pack is ordered by first use from the start scene; with prune it holds only what the scenes use and what the project's Export.AlwaysInclude names (project.setExportSettings), and excludedAssets lists what it left out. The game runs the script module the editor has loaded (build it first with script.build). The manifest carries the game's identity (project.setGameInfo: the title its window shows, version, company, copyright) and, with an icon, icon names <File>.png next to it, 256 x 256 pixels, made from the icon's image (it fails when that does not decode). On Linux hosts a game with the runtime gets <File>.desktop too, a desktop entry naming the export's absolute paths. Returns the files (icon and desktopEntry: null without one), assetCount, the pack's size, seconds, warnings (an enlarged icon, a desktop entry left out) and frameTimes (the editor's frames from the one that started the export to its end, like editor.wait's).
commands.name: project.export

cookDocuments.description: Put scenes, prefabs and models into the pack in their binary cooked form, which loads without parsing JSON (default true; false keeps their JSON)

directory.description: Absolute output directory outside the project (created when missing)

includeScriptSymbols.description: Copy the script module's debug symbols (PDB) too (default: true, false in Dist builds)

prune.description: Leave out assets no scene uses and Export.AlwaysInclude does not name (default false: scripts may load assets by path)

runtime.description: Runtime executable to copy (default: StrataRuntime next to the editor)

commands.description: The running export (project.export) or the last one: {running, state (WaitingForImports, Packing, Copying, Succeeded, Failed, Cancelled), progress (0 to 1), stage (what it does, or how it ended), directory}; {running: false, state: null} before the first.
commands.name: project.exportStatus

commands.description: The open project: name, path (the project file), directories, start scene, export settings, the game's identity (game: title, version, company, copyright, icon; project.setGameInfo) and fileState (written, writing, or unwritten when its last write failed, with fileError: project.save writes it again) ({open: false} without a project).
commands.name: project.info

commands.description: Opens a project file or the project in a directory. Fails while the edited scene has unsaved changes, or the open project's file unwritten settings (its last write failed: project.save), unless force is true (save first); waits for saves in flight (scene.save, the project file) first, also with force. The project opens at once; its start scene loads in the background like scene.open's (the frames go on, scene.loadStatus reports it) and the command answers once it is the edited scene: {projectFile, discardedChanges and discardedSettings (whether unsaved scene changes or unwritten settings were discarded), settingsProblems ([{section, message}]: settings sections whose stored values are refused, kept as stored while their defaults apply; set or reset them with project.setSettings), startScene (null when the project has none), startSceneOpened, startSceneError (why it was not opened; the project stays open with an empty scene), seconds (the start scene's load), migrated (null, or for a project saved by 0.5.0 or older, which is migrated once before its start scene opens and written as the current version: {collisionLayers: {scenes: those whose layers became the project's, conflicts, unreadable}})}.
commands.name: project.open

force.description: Go on although the edited scene has unsaved changes, discarding them (default false: the command fails instead). Discarded changes are kept as recovery data of the project (scene.recoveryStatus), and the person at the editor is told who discarded them

commands.description: Copies a sample project (project.samples) into a new directory and opens the copy, like project.open; the sample itself stays unchanged. Fails while the edited scene has unsaved changes, or the open project's file unwritten settings, unless force is true (save first), before anything is copied; waits for saves in flight (scene.save, the project file) first.
