commands.name: project.openSample

directory.description: Absolute directory for the copy: created, or an existing empty directory

force.description: Go on although the edited scene has unsaved changes, discarding them (default false: the command fails instead). Discarded changes are kept as recovery data of the project (scene.recoveryStatus), and the person at the editor is told who discarded them

sample.description: The sample's id from project.samples, e.g. "Tetris"

commands.description: The sample projects that come with the editor (finished games to learn from, e.g. Tetris): id, name, description and picture (the absolute path of its PNG, 480x270, or null). Open one with project.openSample, which works on a copy.
commands.name: project.samples

commands.description: Writes the project file now and answers once it is written: the project's settings are written in the background after every change anyway, so this is for after a write failed (editor.status' project fileState "unwritten", fileError says why) once its cause is fixed, and for waiting until the file holds the latest change. Fails with the reason when the write fails. Returns projectFile.
commands.name: project.save

commands.description: Names the project's collision layers and sets which of them collide, as one undo step that leaves the scene saved, and writes the project file in the background (project.save waits for it). The layers are the project's: every scene and prefab uses the same 32 layers, names and matrix (scene.info's settings.physicsLayers shows them as the active scene runs them). layerNames apply first, then resetLayerCollisions, then layerCollisions in order; an invalid request changes nothing. Allowed while playing: the running game takes the new table at once (replacing what its scripts changed with Physics::SetLayersCollide) and the change stays after play.stop. Returns physicsLayers ({names, noCollisions}, pairs by name).
commands.name: project.setCollisionLayers

layerCollisions.description: Changes of the layer matrix, applied in order after layerNames: whether two layers (indices 0-31 or names) collide. Every pair collides by default; bodies and character controllers collide only when their layers do

layers.description: The two layers (the same twice: a layer with itself)

layerNames.description: Names of collision layers by index ("0" to "31"), e.g. {"1": "Player", "2": "Debris"}; "" or null clears a name. Names are unique (ignoring case), at most 64 characters, and RigidBody.Layer, CharacterController.Layer, scripts' Physics::GetLayerIndex and layerCollisions accept them

resetLayerCollisions.description: Lets every pair of layers collide again before layerCollisions applies

commands.description: Sets how the project exports, as one undo step (the scene stays saved; allowed while playing, where it is not discarded by play.stop), and writes the project file in the background (project.save waits for it); settings left out keep their values. alwaysInclude: assets ("Prefabs/Enemy.stprefab") and folders ("Prefabs") relative to the asset directory that an export with prune keeps, with what they use, although no scene uses them (assets scripts load by path); each must name an asset or a folder of assets. loadingScene: a scene the exported game plays while its start scene loads (null: none, the game shows a cleared frame meanwhile). Returns both settings.
commands.name: project.setExportSettings

alwaysInclude.description: Asset paths and folders relative to the asset directory ('/' separators); empty to keep nothing extra

loadingScene.description: Scene (handle or path) the game plays while its start scene loads; null for none

commands.description: Sets the game's identity, which exported games show: title (the window's title, the log, dialogs; empty: the project's name), version (one to four whole numbers from 0 to 65535 separated by dots, e.g. "1.2.0"), company and copyright (optional), at most 128 characters of text each without line breaks, and icon: a texture of the project whose source is a PNG, JPEG, TGA or BMP image (at least 256 x 256 pixels, square or centered on transparent pixels), or null for none (the game shows what its platform gives it: on Windows, the runtime's strata mark). Fields left out keep their values. The project's name stays the game's name for its save and log directories, so a new title or company never moves players' saves. One undo step that leaves the scene saved; writes the project file in the background (project.save waits for it); allowed while playing. An invalid field changes nothing. Returns game (title, version, company, copyright, icon).
commands.name: project.setGameInfo

copyright.description: The copyright line, e.g. "(c) 2026 Studio" (empty: none)

icon.description: Texture (handle or path) whose PNG, JPEG, TGA or BMP source becomes the game's icon; null for none

title.description: The game's title (empty: the project's name)

commands.description: Sets one project settings section (project.settings lists them with their schemas) to a value, or with reset: true back to its default, as one undo step that leaves the scene saved, and writes the project file in the background (project.save waits for it). The value replaces the section's whole value (a simple section's fields left out take their defaults) and is checked by the section first: an invalid one changes nothing and fails naming the first bad field. Allowed while playing: the running game reads the change at once and it stays after play.stop. Returns section, value (what applies now) and isDefault.
commands.name: project.setSettings

reset.description: Back to the section's default instead of a value (default false)

value.description: The section's new value, matching its schema (project.settings)

commands.description: Sets the scene a built game starts with, as one undo step (the scene stays saved; allowed while playing, where it is not discarded by play.stop), and writes the project file in the background (editor.status' project fileState; project.save waits for it). When it is the export settings' loading scene (project.setExportSettings), that setting is cleared (loadingSceneCleared: true), as the loading scene plays while the start scene loads. Returns startScene and loadingSceneCleared.
commands.name: project.setStartScene

scene.description: Start scene (asset handle, or path relative to the asset directory)

commands.description: The project's settings: its own fields (project: name, startScene, loadingScene, alwaysInclude, game: the game's identity; set with project.setStartScene, project.setExportSettings and project.setGameInfo) and every project settings section the engine's modules and the game register (sections: id, title, category, description, version, schema: the JSON Schema of its value, value: what applies, isDefault: whether the project leaves it at its default, problem: why a stored value is refused, null when none), in registration order; unclaimed lists sections the file stores that no module of this editor claims (kept as stored). section narrows sections to one. Set one with project.setSettings.
commands.name: project.settings

section.description: A section's id ("<Module>.<Name>") to describe alone

commands.description: The templates project.create and scene.new accept: id, name and what a project made from it contains. "basic3d" starts lit (camera, sun, procedural sky, ground, post-processing); "empty" is the default and has no scene.
commands.name: project.templates

commands.description: Every entity of the active scene in hierarchy order, with parent, depth and component names.
commands.name: scene.hierarchy

commands.description: Name, asset, modification and play state, entity count and settings of the edited scene, and what runs while playing (running: the running scene, which a game's scene switch makes another than the edited one; null in edit mode; see play.state). entityCount counts the active scene's entities (the running one while playing); settings.physicsLayers are the project's collision layers as the active scene runs them. settings.fixedRate is the step the active scene runs: source project when the project's Scene.Timing FixedRate sets it (project.setSettings), scene for its own fixedTimestep.
commands.name: scene.info

commands.description: Loads a scene asset into the running game next to what it holds (a sub-scene, as scripts' Scene::LoadAdditive does; play mode only: play.stop ends it with the game). The scene and everything it uses load in the background, then its entities are created over the following frames (at most the scene's maxEntitiesInstantiatedPerFrame per frame), keeping their IDs: a sub-scene whose IDs the running scene has already (the same scene twice) fails. Answers once every entity exists: {subScene (its number, for scene.unloadAdditive), scene, state, progress, createdEntities, skippedEntities, totalEntities, slices, roots (the top-level entities), seconds, frames}. scene.loadStatus reports sub-scenes while they load.
commands.name: scene.loadAdditive

scene.description: Scene asset to load into the running scene (asset handle, or path relative to the asset directory)

commands.description: The scene loads under way: open (the scene scene.open, or project.open for the project's start scene, is opening: {scene, startScene, state: LoadingScene | LoadingDependencies | Preparing (its render proxies are built for the viewport), progress 0 to 1}, null when none), lastOpen (the latest of those that finished: {scene, startScene, state: Ready | Failed | Cancelled, error, seconds}, null before the first), play (the scene a running game asked for while it loads, {scene, progress}, null when none) and subScenes (the running scene's sub-scenes, scene.loadAdditive: {subScene, scene, state: Loading | Instantiating | Loaded | Failed, progress, createdEntities, skippedEntities (not created because an ancestor was deleted while the sub-scene loaded), totalEntities, slices, error}) and world (the cells the open world streams around the editor camera, editor, and while playing those of the running game, game: each {cellsWanted, cellsLoading, cellsLoaded, cellsUnloading, cellsPinned, cellsFailed} or null; null when no world streams). With wait, it answers once no scene is being opened, e.g. after starting an editor with a window, which opens its project's start scene in the background (scene edits and play.start fail until then).
commands.name: scene.loadStatus

wait.description: Answer once no scene is being opened (default false: at once)

commands.description: Replaces the edited scene with a new, unsaved one: empty by default, or with a template's content, e.g. "basic3d" (a lit start: camera, sun, procedural sky, ground, post-processing; the editor camera then looks through the scene's camera; the ground's material Materials/Ground.stmat is added to a project that lacks it). Fails while the edited scene has unsaved changes unless force is true (save first). Save the new scene with scene.saveAs. Waits for saves in flight (scene.save) first. Returns discardedChanges (whether unsaved changes were discarded).
commands.name: scene.new

force.description: Go on although the edited scene has unsaved changes, discarding them (default false: the command fails instead). Discarded changes are kept as recovery data of the project (scene.recoveryStatus), and the person at the editor is told who discarded them

template.description: What the scene starts with (default "empty"; see project.templates)

commands.description: Opens a scene asset for editing. Fails while the edited scene has unsaved changes unless force is true (save first); waits for saves in flight (scene.save) before it decides. The scene is read and loaded with everything it uses in the background while the editor goes on showing the edited scene, which stays read-only meanwhile (edits and play.start fail); the command answers once the opened scene replaced it: {scene, name, entities, discardedChanges (whether unsaved changes were discarded), seconds, frames, frameTimes (the CPU time of the frames that ran meanwhile: count, medianMs, meanMs, p95Ms, maxMs)}. Opening another scene, scene.new or closing the project cancels it. scene.loadStatus (and editor.status's sceneLoad) report its progress.
commands.name: scene.open

force.description: Go on although the edited scene has unsaved changes, discarding them (default false: the command fails instead). Discarded changes are kept as recovery data of the project (scene.recoveryStatus), and the person at the editor is told who discarded them

scene.description: Scene to open (asset handle, or path relative to the asset directory)

commands.description: What a ray, or a pixel of the Scene view, hits among what the active scene draws: its mesh renderers, on their triangles (their bounds while a mesh loads). Give origin and direction, or viewport {x, y, width?, height?} (a pixel of the Scene view's image, through its camera: the editor camera, or the scene's primary camera with Game camera on). maxDistance limits the ray (default: unlimited for origin and direction, the view's far plane for a pixel); ignore leaves entities out with their descendants. Returns {hit: true, entity, name, point, normal (facing the ray's origin), distance, onTriangle (false: a loading mesh's bounds were hit), ray: {origin, direction}} or {hit: false, ray}; ray is what asset.place {ray} takes. Colliders, gizmos and UI are not hit. While playing it casts into the running game.
commands.name: scene.raycast

direction.description: Where the ray points, any length but zero (with origin)

ignore.description: Entities left out, with their descendants (entity IDs)

maxDistance.description: How far along the ray to look, in meters (default: unlimited for a ray, the view's far plane for a pixel)

origin.description: Where the ray starts, in world space (with direction)

viewport.description: A pixel of the Scene view's image, cast through its camera (instead of origin and direction)

height.description: The height of that image (default: the Scene view's, or 720)

width.description: The width of the image the pixel refers to (default: the Scene view's, or 1280 while it has none)

x.description: Pixels from the image's left edge, continuous: the middle of the first column is 0.5

y.description: Pixels from the image's top edge, continuous

commands.description: Applies or discards recovery data (scene.recoveryStatus). apply: opens the scene the changes were made to in the background as scene.open does (a scene never saved: a new scene of its name) and, once it is in, turns it into what the edits left, as one undo step back to the saved scene (a world's changes wait until the cells they name are loaded, and go back into them); the scene stays modified (save it to keep the changes). It refuses when the scene file changed since the changes were made (applicable false), while playing, while a scene is being opened (scene.loadStatus), and while the edited scene has unsaved changes it would discard unless force is true; it waits for saves in flight (scene.save) first. discard: moves the data to .strata/Recovery/Discarded, where it is not offered again. Returns {recovered | discarded: id, ...}; apply also scene, sceneName, entities (how many it restored or removed) and discardedChanges.
commands.name: scene.recover

force.description: Go on although the edited scene has unsaved changes, discarding them (default false: the command fails instead). Discarded changes are kept as recovery data of the project (scene.recoveryStatus), and the person at the editor is told who discarded them

scene.description: The id of an entry of scene.recoveryStatus, or a scene asset (handle or path) to use its newest applicable entry

commands.description: The recovery data of the open project (.strata/Recovery): unsaved scene changes an editor left behind when it ended without closing the scene (a crash), or that were discarded on purpose (force, Don't Save) and kept anyway. Returns entries, newest first, each {id, scene (null for a scene never saved), sceneName, scenePath, time (milliseconds since 1970-01-01 UTC), discarded, entityCount, complete (a snapshot of every entity), applicable, problem (why it cannot be applied, e.g. the scene was saved since)}, and the journal of the edited scene {active, file, writes, lastWrite, pending (changes not written yet: they are written about 2 s after edits stop), pendingSteps (undo steps waiting for that write), busy, skipped (why its changes are not journaled)}. Reads the directory again, after the journal writes already asked for; while the project's assets are scanned it answers once they are (entries are judged against them). Apply or discard an entry with scene.recover. Fails without a project.
commands.name: scene.recoveryStatus

commands.description: Saves the edited scene to its asset in the background and answers once the file is written (wait false: at once). The frame only takes a snapshot of the scene, the document is written on a background thread, and edits made meanwhile stay unsaved (the save holds the scene as it was when the command ran). With wait (default true) the answer comes once the file is written and published: {scene, path, bytes, entities, seconds, frames, frameTimes (the editor's frames meanwhile: count, medianMs, meanMs, p95Ms, maxMs), memory {privateMBBefore, peakPrivateMBDuring}}. With wait false it answers at once with {scene, path, saveId, state: Writing | Queued}; editor.status's saving lists the saves in flight. A save queues behind one that writes. New scenes need scene.saveAs first. A world's persistent scene saves the documents changed since the last save, in the background too: the persistent scene (without the cells' entities), each dirty cell and then the world's document with those cells' index entries; documents lists them ({path, kind: persistent, cell or world, bytes, entities}; bytes and entities are their sums), and a world's save waits for its previous one.
commands.name: scene.save

wait.description: Answer once the document is written (default true); false answers at once with the save's saveId

commands.description: Saves the edited scene as a new .stscene asset and continues editing it: the scene takes the file's name and the new asset at once (a following scene.save writes it), and gets the previous ones back when the save fails. The save runs in the background like scene.save's and answers like it (wait, default true: once written; false: at once with its saveId).
commands.name: scene.saveAs

path.description: Path relative to the asset directory, e.g. "Scenes/Level1.stscene"

wait.description: Answer once the document is written (default true); false answers at once with the save's saveId

commands.description: Changes settings of the edited scene: gravity, the fixed step, the physics world's capacities, and how many entities additive loads (sub-scenes) create per frame (undoable, one step). Capacities take effect when a physics world is created, at the next play start, so set them in edit mode. While playing, changes go to the running copy only and play.stop discards them (the result then has a warning). Collision layers are the project's: set them with project.setCollisionLayers. The project's fixed rate (Scene.Timing, project.setSettings) overrides fixedTimestep and maxFixedStepsPerFrame; they apply when its FixedRate is Scene (a change is stored either way, with a warning). Returns the settings with the step the scene runs (fixedRate) and the collision layers it runs with (scene.info shows them too).
commands.name: scene.setSettings

fixedTimestep.description: Fixed simulation step in seconds (1/1000 to 1/10)

layerCollisions.description: Refused since 0.6.0: collision layers are the project's, set with project.setCollisionLayers (same parameter)

layerNames.description: Refused since 0.6.0: collision layers are the project's, set with project.setCollisionLayers (same parameter)

maxEntitiesDestroyedPerFrame.description: Entities sub-scenes being unloaded (scene.unloadAdditive, scripts' SubScene::Unload, a world's cells) may destroy per frame, all together (default 5000); creation and destruction together stop after about 2 ms a frame

maxEntitiesInstantiatedPerFrame.description: Entities sub-scenes loading into the scene (scene.loadAdditive, scripts' Scene::LoadAdditive) may create per frame, all together (default 5000); each frame also stops creating after about 2 ms

maxFixedStepsPerFrame.description: Upper bound of fixed steps per frame

physicsCapacity.description: Physics world room (only the given values change), reserved when play starts (up to 131072 bodies and 262144 contacts at once; beyond that it counts for growth only); raise it for scenes that create many bodies while they play, so that the world does not grow during play

maxBodies.description: Bodies the physics world has room for when play starts (each about 2 KiB); 0 sizes it from the bodies the scene starts with. The world grows beyond it while bodies are created

maxBodyPairs.description: Ignored since 0.5.0 (box3d has no buffer of body pairs to size); accepted for older command scripts, with a warning

maxContactConstraints.description: Contacts the physics world has room for when play starts (each about 250 bytes); 0: automatic

resetLayerCollisions.description: Refused since 0.6.0: collision layers are the project's, set with project.setCollisionLayers (same parameter)

commands.description: Removes a sub-scene from the running game (play mode only): stops its load, releasing what it held loaded, and takes its entities out of the game at once (inactive: no rendering, scripts' updates, physics or audio); they are destroyed with their descendants over the following frames (at most the scene's maxEntitiesDestroyedPerFrame a frame; their scripts get OnDestroy; scene.loadStatus shows the sub-scene Unloading with destroyedEntities until its last entity is gone). Returns {subScene, entities (the running scene's count now), unloadingEntities (those still to destroy)}.
commands.name: scene.unloadAdditive

commands.description: Attaches a script class of the loaded module to an entity, optionally overriding fields (undoable; while playing it changes the running copy only and the script starts at once). Needs a loaded module (script.build) to check the class and field types.
commands.name: script.add

class.description: Script class name as registered with ST_SCRIPT_CLASS (see script.status)

fields.description: Field overrides by name, e.g. {"Speed": 2.5, "Target": "<entity id>", "Prefab": "Prefabs/Bullet.stprefab"}

commands.description: Builds the project's scripts (the CMakeLists.txt in its Scripts directory) with the engine's compiler and configuration, then loads the module, or hot-reloads it when it changed (playing scenes keep their script state and get OnReload). One build runs at a time; a second request fails while one runs. Fails with the first compiler errors; the result and script.status list all diagnostics (file, line, message) and the end of the build log.
commands.name: script.build

wait.description: Return when the build finished, with its result (default true); false returns at once (poll script.status)

commands.description: Writes a new script class into the project's script directory: a .cpp with the class (deriving from Script), its ST_SCRIPT_CLASS registration and, with the behaviour template (default), OnCreate, OnUpdate and an example field (Speed) or the fields given. The class name must be a C++ identifier that neither the project's scripts nor the SDK declare. Creates the script build first when the project has none (script.init). Build it with script.build before attaching it (script.add accepts classes of the loaded module only); afterwards play.start rebuilds sources that changed. Returns the file written (absolute and relative to the project) and the class.
commands.name: script.create

class.description: The class name, a C++ identifier, e.g. PlayerController

fields.description: Fields to declare, by name, with their type: bool, int, float, vec2, vec3, vec4, quat, string, entity, asset (case does not matter), e.g. {"Speed": "float", "Target": "entity"}

open.description: Also open the new file in the external editor (default false)

path.description: Where to write it, relative to the script directory and ending in .cpp (default: <class>.cpp); folders are created

template.description: behaviour (default): OnCreate, OnUpdate and fields; empty: only the class and its registration

commands.description: The field values of the scripts attached to an entity. While the game plays they are the live instances' values (game state kept in fields, e.g. a score, as it is now; live: true); otherwise the values the scene stores (overrides, else the class defaults). known: false means the loaded module has no such class, so only stored overrides are listed. Optionally one class.
commands.name: script.get

class.description: Only this script class (default: every script of the entity)

commands.description: Creates the project's script build if it is missing: the CMakeLists.txt in its Scripts directory (new projects have it already), the CMakePresets.json IDEs read (the engine's toolchain and STRATA_ENGINE_DIR, for IntelliSense; rewritten when Strata wrote it and the toolchain changed) and, with example, an example script (Spinner.cpp). Other existing files are kept. Returns the files written.
commands.name: script.init

example.description: Also write the example script (default false)

commands.description: Lists the project's script sources, the files the script build compiles: the code and CMake files of its script directory (folders starting with '.' and build trees left out), sorted by path, each with the script classes it registers (ST_SCRIPT_CLASS) and its size. Use it to find the file that holds a class before changing it (script.open opens one in the person's code editor). Returns sourceDirectory, files [{path (relative to the script directory), projectPath (relative to the project), classes, bytes}] and truncated (more files than listed, or the folder could not be listed completely).
commands.name: script.list

commands.description: Loads a script module file instead of the project's built one (e.g. a module built outside the editor). Playing scenes switch to it like on a hot reload. The project's own module is loaded again by script.build.
commands.name: script.load

path.description: Module file (.dll/.so/.dylib): absolute, or relative to the project directory

commands.description: Opens a script source in the person's code editor at a line (e.g. a compiler diagnostic or a crash location from script.status): the external editor command (script.setExternalEditor, or STRATA_EXTERNAL_EDITOR), else the system's default application for the file. Without file, the project's script directory opens. Only code, CMake and text files of the project or the engine. Returns what opened it.
commands.name: script.open

file.description: The file: relative to the project directory, or absolute (as diagnostics name them)

commands.description: Loads the script module's file again (hot reload: playing scenes keep their script state and get OnReload), or the project's built module when none is loaded. Also clears a crash fault.
commands.name: script.reload

commands.description: Detaches a script from an entity by class name (undoable; while playing it changes the running copy only and the script gets OnDestroy). Works without a loaded module.
commands.name: script.remove

commands.description: Sets the person's code editor, which script.open, the Problems panel and crash reports use: a command template such as "code -g {file}:{line}:{column}" or "\"C:/Program Files/.../devenv.exe\" /Edit {file}" (whitespace separates arguments, double quotes group them; {file}, {line}, {column} and {directory} are filled in; without {file} the file goes last). The program runs directly, never through a shell: a path, or a name found in PATH (VS Code's code launcher starts Code.exe), not a .cmd or .bat; a program that is not there is refused. An empty command goes back to the default application. Kept in the person's preferences (the Editor.ExternalEditor section of preferences.get, not the project); STRATA_EXTERNAL_EDITOR overrides it. Returns the command in use and the program the person's command starts (program).
commands.name: script.setExternalEditor

command.description: The command template, or empty for none

commands.description: Overrides one field of a script attached to an entity, or resets it to the class default with value null (undoable; while playing it changes the running copy and the live script at once). The value must fit the field's type (see script.status): bool, integer, number, [x, y] / [x, y, z] / [x, y, z, w] arrays, quaternions as [x, y, z, w] or Euler degrees [pitch, yaw, roll], text, an entity ID, or an asset handle or path. Needs a loaded module (script.build) to check the field.
commands.name: script.setField

value.description: New value, or null to use the class default

commands.description: The project's scripts: the loaded module (path, load count, hot reload), its classes with their fields (name, type, default) and implemented callbacks, the current crash fault and the last one that stopped play mode, the running and last build (with compiler diagnostics and the toolchain it used), and the toolchain the next build uses (an installed editor finds one on this machine at its first build: toolchain.found).
commands.name: script.status

commands.description: The selected entities (the last one is the primary selection) and the asset the inspector shows instead of them (inspectedAsset, null while the entities are inspected).
commands.name: selection.get

commands.description: Replaces the selection of entities (an empty array clears it; selecting entities shows them in the inspector) and/or shows an asset in the asset inspector (asset; null returns to the entities), as clicking it in the Content Browser does. The entities stay selected while an asset is inspected.
commands.name: selection.set

asset.description: Asset to inspect (handle or path), or null for the entities

commands.description: Creates a game UI element ready to use, in one undo step (while playing it changes the running copy only): a canvas, a panel (a rounded, framed background), an image, a text, a button (with its label), a toggle (with box, checkmark and label), a slider (with track, fill and handle), an input field (a line the player types into, with its text and placeholder; Enter calls OnUISubmit) or a horizontal, vertical or grid layout group. An element whose parent is outside every canvas (or that has none) gets a new top-level canvas first. anchor places it on its parent (and sets the pivot to match); position and size are in canvas units (along a stretched axis size is added to the parent's span: 0 fills it). Returns entity, canvas, created (every new entity), parts (label, background, fill, handle, checkmark, placeholder, as the type has them) and rect ([x, y, width, height] in pixels at the game's screen).
commands.name: ui.create

anchor.description: Where it sits on its parent: topLeft, topCenter, topRight, topStretch, middleLeft, middleCenter, middleRight, middleStretch, bottomLeft, bottomCenter, bottomRight, bottomStretch, stretchLeft, stretchCenter, stretchRight, stretch (default middleCenter)

name.description: The element's name (default: the type's, e.g. "Button")

parent.description: The parent (a canvas or an element of one; outside a canvas a new canvas is made) (entity ID or null)

position.description: [x, y]: the pivot's offset from the anchors in canvas units, +y down (default [0, 0])

size.description: [width, height] in canvas units (default: the type's; along stretched axes 0)

text.description: The text of a text, button or toggle, or an input field's placeholder (default "New Text", "Button", "Toggle", "Enter text...")

type.description: What to create: canvas, panel, image, text, button, toggle, slider, inputField, horizontalLayout, verticalLayout, gridLayout

commands.description: What the player would hit at a position of the game's screen (edit and play mode): the topmost raycast target (an image or text that is one, or a selectable) of the canvases that receive input, as entity, name, path (from its canvas), selectable (the selectable it belongs to, which a click would press) and interactable; entity null when the position hits nothing. World-space canvases are hit where the scene's camera looks through the position, after every screen-space canvas. With all, every element whose rect contains the position, topmost first, raycast target or not, in every canvas.
commands.name: ui.hitTest

all.description: List every element at the position instead (default false)

position.description: [x, y] in screen pixels from the top-left corner

screen.description: [width, height] of the screen in pixels (default: the game's screen: while playing the game view's image, in edit mode the viewport's image, without either 1920x1080)

commands.description: Where the game UI's elements are at a screen size, without rendering: the root canvases (entity, name, scale in pixels per canvas unit, unitSize, sortOrder, receivesInput) and the elements of an entity's subtree (all canvases without one), in draw order: entity, name, rect ([x, y, width, height] in screen pixels; on a canvas in the scene (worldSpace) in canvas units, with screenRect where the scene's camera shows it), visible, visibleRect for elements under a UI Mask (what its clip rect leaves of the rect: where it is drawn and clicked), and for selectables interactable, state (normal, hover, pressed, focused, disabled) and focused, for texts and input fields text (and editing for a field the player types into), for sliders and toggles value. At most 1,000 elements (truncated tells). Check that a HUD keeps its proportions by comparing rects at several screens.
commands.name: ui.layout

entity.description: A canvas or element whose subtree to list (default: every canvas) (entity ID or null)

screen.description: [width, height] of the screen in pixels (default: the game's screen: while playing the game view's image, in edit mode the viewport's image, without either 1920x1080)

commands.description: Renders the scene on the next frame and returns the picture as a PNG image, with its width and height. By default it looks like the viewport: its size (1280x720 while the viewport is hidden), the scene's primary camera while playing (the editor camera otherwise) and the editor overlays (grid, selection outline, light/camera/collider shapes) for the editor camera; camera "scene" takes the Game view's size when it keeps an aspect ratio or a fixed size (viewport.setSettings gameView). position, target and fov look through a camera of the capture's own (the editor camera with those changes; camera.get stays as it was): position + target looks from one at the other, either alone moves the editor camera's view keeping its direction; the result's camera is then "custom", and view has the position, forward direction and fov used. With the editor camera outside play mode, a scene without any light of its own is lit by preview lighting (previewLighting: true in the result; the game will be unlit) and the game's screen-space text and UI canvases are hidden (hiddenScreenSpaceTexts and ui.hiddenCanvases count them): see viewport.setSettings, or use camera "scene" to see what the game shows. ui reports the game UI drawn: {canvases, hiddenCanvases, elements, drawCalls, pendingGlyphs}. Text and UI whose glyphs are still being prepared delay the picture by a few frames, so they are complete, and so do meshes, materials and textures of the view that are still loading (waitForAssets, default true: up to about five seconds of frames; waitedFrames counts the extra renders), and textures it draws that still lack the finer mip levels the view wants (up to about two seconds, as a texture budget may keep them out), and animators that animate only while seen (WhenVisible) until they show the pose of their time (a few frames, also while paused), and mesh renderers the scene just gained until they reached the GPU (a few frames for a million; renderStats.deferredInstanceBytes says what still waited), and the renderer's pre-exposure (the power of two its HDR values are scaled by, chosen from automatic exposure's metering read back frames later) until it settled (a few frames, also without waitForAssets; preExposureSettled false if it did not within 8), and a scene drawn with temporal anti-aliasing (PostProcess AntiAliasingMethod TAA), also without waitForAssets, until 8 frames of the complete view, the mean of its jitter's phases (temporalFrames: the frames the picture's history holds, 0 without it). Reports what was still loading when the picture was taken (pendingAssets), the textures drawn coarser than the view wants (texturesBelowWanted), animators drawn with an older pose (stalePoses), glyphs that could not be prepared in time (pendingTextGlyphs) and point and spot lights' shadow views not drawn (localShadowViewsPending; captures draw them all at once) and reflection probes whose capture was not loaded (reflectionProbesPending; waited for as assets are, with waitForAssets; captures convert loaded ones at once), and whether spatial screen-space reflections still lacked a previous frame's color (screenSpaceReflectionsPending). Every wait is bounded and the command succeeds when a bound runs out: complete is true when the picture lacks nothing, else incomplete lists the JSON pointers of the result's fields that say what it lacks ("/pendingAssets", "/preExposureSettled", "/temporalFrames" under TAA, "/debugView/shadows/complete", "/notice" when the view fell back to another camera, ...). debugView colors the picture by streaming state, level of detail, mip levels, motion or shadow texels, or shows a lighting view (default: the viewport's, viewport.setSettings) and the result's debugView says what it found: {view, tintedEntities, pendingEntities, failedEntities, placeholderBoxes, entitiesPerLOD: [LOD0, LOD1, LOD2, LOD3+], lodErrorPixels: [the largest error drawn at each of those, in pixels, where levels are chosen by their errors; else 0], entitiesPerMipShortfall: [at the wanted level, 1 level coarser, 2, 3+ or loading]} among the entities in view; with "shadows" also shadows: {complete, shadowMapSize, surfaceShare, skyShare, uncoveredShare (of the image), median/p10/p90PixelsPerTexel, aboveFourShare (of covered receivers), cascades: [{index, near, far, texelSize, screenShare, median/p10/p90PixelsPerTexel, aboveFourShare}]}; with a lighting view debugView.lighting holds what it measured (EV100 percentiles, albedo shares, sunToSkyRatio). renderStats is what the captured frame drew, as editor.perf's renderStats (draws, instances, shadow casters, triangles, proxies, lights, timings), with gpuMs: the GPU's milliseconds per stage of the captured frame (empty, with gpuStatsFrame null, where the GPU writes no timestamps). quality draws the picture at a preset (default: the view's); renderStats.quality says what it drew with. Needs a GPU (fails in editors started with --no-gpu). live: true renders nothing: it reads back what the Scene view (camera "editor") or the Game view ("scene") presented, as it played, to see motion (trails, smearing, crawling) at exact steps: arm it after play.start {paused: true}, then run input.sequence or play.step. It fails when the view does not render, play stops or step atFixedStep already ran; images: [{fixedSteps, temporalFrames, width, height, path}]. renderer switches techniques of the renderer for this one picture, to show what they do (SpecularAntiAliasing, SpecularEnergyCompensation, DitherOutput, GPUDriven, OcclusionCulling, SpatialReflectionResolve, FXAASubpixel 0.75, GlobalIlluminationBounceGain 0 for one bounce, ...): it renders through a renderer of its own, so no view of the editor or game frame changes; the result's renderer echoes the switches set.
commands.name: viewport.capture

atFixedStep.description: live: the first frame the view renders once the game's fixedSteps reached this

camera.description: "editor": the editor camera; "scene": the scene's primary camera (fails without one)

debugView.description: "streaming" tints entities by streaming state (pending Sulfur, failed Cinnabar, missing meshes as boxes), "lod" by level of detail, "mip" by the mip levels their textures lack, "motion" colors pixels by their motion since the capture's previous frame (rendered twice for it: still scenes show none), "shadows" colors receivers by screen pixels per shadow texel and outlines the cascades; "lighting" white surfaces, "ao" ambient occlusion, "indirect" indirect light only, "luminance" EV100 bands, "albedo" base colors (outside 0.03-0.85 marked), each with debugView.lighting: {view, surfaceShare, surfaceEv100 {p05, p50, p95}, backgroundEv100, value {median, p05} (ao, albedo), belowRangeShare, aboveRangeShare (albedo), sunIlluminance, skyIlluminance (lux on flat ground), sunToSkyRatio}; "voxels" the GI's voxels, with debugView.globalIllumination {ran, settled, voxelLevels, memoryMiB}; "specular" and "diffuse" the light of one kind (no emission, no fog), "clusters" the lights each pixel's light cluster lists as bands (none, 1, 2-3, 4-7, ...; debugView.lighting.value: shares of a cluster's capacity); "culled" boxes of the mesh renderers in view that culling left out (too small: Sulfur, about 6 pixels across; hidden behind what is drawn: Cinnabar, the GPU-driven path's occlusion culling; renderStats.sizeCulledProxies counts the first, occludedProxies all found hidden, also those the frame drew once more while the camera moves), "wireframe" the edges of every triangle drawn over the image (it needs the device's non-solid fill mode: without it the lines are left out and the log says why); "none" not at all (default: the viewport's debug view)

fov.description: Vertical field of view in degrees of the capture's own camera

frames.description: live: that frame and the next ones, as numbered files beside path above 1 (default 1)

height.description: Image height in pixels; without width the viewport's aspect ratio is kept

live.description: Return what the view (camera: required) presented, with its history as it is, instead of rendering

overlays.description: Draw the editor overlays enabled in the viewport (default: on for the editor camera, off for the scene camera)

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file at path (default false: an existing file is an error)

path.description: Also save the PNG to this .png file: relative to the project directory (needs an open project) or absolute; folders are created, network and device paths are refused

position.description: Look from this point (a camera of the capture's own; the editor camera does not move)

quality.description: The quality the picture is drawn at (default: the quality of the view it shows: the Scene view's for the editor camera and cameras of the capture's own, the game's for the scene's camera: the project's, with the players' options while playing)

renderer.description: Switches of the renderer for this capture alone, named as SceneRendererSpecification's fields, to show what a technique does (e.g. {"SpecularAntiAliasing": false}); the editor's views, other captures and the game never draw with them. Unset ones keep the capture's own values. Automatic exposure meters each capture alone: compare switches that change the light with a fixed exposure

BatchAcrossMaterials.description: Instances of a mesh share draws whatever their materials (false: the CPU path splits them by material)

DitherOutput.description: The 8-bit output is dithered (false shows the banding of gradients)

FXAASubpixel.description: FXAA's sub-pixel aliasing removal: 0.25 (the default) or 0.75

FadeLevelsOfDetail.description: Levels of detail cross-fade over a few frames instead of switching (captures: off)

GPUDriven.description: The GPU-driven path where the device has it (true, the default) or the CPU path (false)

GlobalIlluminationBounceGain.description: The share of last frame's light global illumination bounces again (1, the default; 0: one bounce)

HorizonFade.description: Reflections a normal map turns into the surface fade out

OcclusionCulling.description: GPU-driven frames leave out what lies behind what the view draws

SpatialReflectionResolve.description: Spatial screen-space reflections are resolved over 5x5 pixels (false: each pixel's traced reflection as the march found it)

SpecularAntiAliasing.description: Specular lobes widen by how much the shading normal changes across a pixel

SpecularEnergyCompensation.description: Specular light is compensated for multiple scattering (false: the single-scattering lobe, darker on rough surfaces)

TextureStreaming.description: Textures stream at the levels the screen needs (false: every texture drawn is made resident whole)

VisibilityFeedback.description: GPU-driven frames take their asset requests from the GPU's visibility feedback

target.description: Look at this point (a camera of the capture's own; the editor camera does not move)

waitForAssets.description: Render again on the following frames while assets of the view are still loading, up to about five seconds, while textures lack the mip levels the view wants, up to about two, and while new mesh renderers are on their way to the GPU (default true); false takes the picture at once

width.description: Image width in pixels; without height the viewport's aspect ratio is kept

commands.description: The viewport's view settings (saved with the project's editor state): which editor overlays are drawn (grid, selectionOutline, sceneGizmos, stats; allColliders: collider shapes of every entity instead of only the selection's), previewLighting (editor views light scenes without any light of their own with a preview sun and sky), gameUI (editor views draw the game's screen-space UI, its HUD text and UI canvases, and a click selects a UI element), canvasMode (the 2D canvas mode for placing game UI), the gizmo mode and space, whether gizmo drags snap, the snap steps, debugView ("none", or "streaming" / "lod" / "mip" / "motion" / "shadows": the image colored by streaming state, level of detail, the mip levels textures lack, motion or shadow texels per pixel; or a lighting view: "lighting", "ao", "indirect", "luminance", "albedo", or global illumination's "voxels", "gi", "open", "probes"; "specular" and "diffuse" the light of one kind, "clusters" the lights each pixel's light cluster lists; "culled" boxes of what culling left out, "wireframe" the triangles' edges), gameView (the Game view's image: {mode, width, height}, width and height for mode "custom"), pilotGameCamera (the Scene view looks through the scene's primary camera) and editPose ("rest" or "clipStart": what skinned characters of the edited scene show while it does not play).
commands.name: viewport.getSettings

commands.description: Changes view settings of the viewport (a view change: no undo step, the scene is unchanged) and returns all of them like viewport.getSettings. Editor views are the Scene view's editor camera (also while the game plays); the Game view and the scene's camera always show the scene as the game does.
commands.name: viewport.setSettings

allColliders.description: Draw the collider shapes of every entity; off (the default), only those of the selection and its descendants

canvasMode.description: The 2D canvas mode (edit mode): the viewport shows the selection's UI canvas (else the first) at its reference aspect ratio through the scene's camera with the game UI, with handles to move and resize UI elements

cellBounds.description: While a world is open (or the game streams one), draw the squares of its cells loading (Sulfur), loaded (Ochre) and unloading (gray) around the camera

debugView.description: Color every view of the viewport: "streaming" tints entities whose mesh, material or textures are still loading (Sulfur; failed ones Cinnabar; entities whose mesh is not there are drawn as boxes), "lod" tints entities by the level of detail they are drawn at (0 to 3+), "mip" tints entities with textures by the mip levels their worst texture lacks against what their view needs (none Malachite, 1 Azurite, 2 Sulfur, 3 or more or still loading Cinnabar), "motion" colors every pixel by its motion since the view's previous frame (hue: the direction, right red, up yellow-green, left cyan, down violet; strength: the speed, full at 16 pixels a frame; still pixels darkened), "shadows" colors receivers by screen pixels per shadow texel (green at most 1, yellow 2, red 4 and more), outlines the sun's cascades and hatches their blend bands, "lighting" shades every lit surface white (the light alone), "ao" shows the occlusion that darkens indirect light (white: none), "indirect" only the sky's, probes' and reflected light, "luminance" the scene's luminance in EV100 bands (log2 nits + 3; the legend names them), "albedo" the base colors with values below 0.03 marked Azurite and above 0.85 striped Cinnabar, "voxels" global illumination's voxels: the scene as the GI sees it, each surface its voxels' albedo, two-sided voxels (no bounce) Cinnabar, "gi" global illumination's diffuse light on white surfaces (its field near the camera, today's light beyond), "open" the share of the sky each surface sees through the world as gray, "probes" its first cascade's probes, dead ones (inside solids) dark red, "specular" only the specular light (the lights' highlights and image light's reflections) and "diffuse" only the diffuse light, both without emission and fog, "clusters" how many lights each pixel's light cluster lists (bands: none, 1, 2-3, 4-7, ...; what its shading walks), "culled" the bounds of the mesh renderers in view that culling left out, as boxes over everything: Sulfur those too small on screen (grown to about 6 pixels across), Cinnabar those hidden behind what is drawn (occlusion culling, on the GPU-driven path only), "wireframe" the edges of every triangle drawn (all levels of detail, skins as posed) over the image, "none" shows the image as rendered

editPose.description: What skinned characters of the edited scene show while it does not play: "rest" (the default) their skeleton's rest pose, "clipStart" the first frame of what they play on start (the controller's default state's clip, else the Animator's Clip; the rest pose without either). animation.preview requests win over both, and play mode is unchanged

gameUI.description: Editor views draw the game's screen-space UI (its HUD text and UI canvases), and a click in the view selects a UI element; off by default so the HUD does not cover the scene

mode.description: The Game view's image: free fills the panel, an aspect ratio is the largest image of it inside the panel (letterboxed), a size renders at exactly those pixels scaled to fit, custom uses width and height, game the resolution the running game asked for (free without a request)

pilotGameCamera.description: The Scene view looks through the scene's primary camera, with the editor's overlays (F8)

previewLighting.description: Editor views light scenes without any light of their own (no directional, point, spot or sky light) with a preview sun and sky (never part of the scene or the game)

quality.description: What the Scene view draws with: the project's Graphics Quality (Renderer.Quality, the default) or a preset of this editor's for the view (a view setting, saved with the editor's state, no undo step); the Game view and the scene's camera always draw at the game's: the project's, and while playing the players' options over it

sceneGizmos.description: Draw light, camera and collider shapes (far away lights and cameras as small icons)

snap.description: Snap gizmo drags to the steps below (holding Ctrl inverts it)

stats.description: Show frame time, draw calls and loading assets over the image

translateSnap.description: Move snapping step in world units

commands.description: Measures a world's cells for its index, off the frame: per cell its entities, physics bodies, bounds and the stored bytes it loads, and the most bodies the persistent scene's streaming sources can keep loaded anywhere (maxBodiesInRadius); writes them into the world document. Only cells whose files changed since the last cook are read again (cellsRead; cellsReused). Fails, writing nothing, when cells share entity IDs with each other or with the persistent scene (the error names them) or a cell cannot be read. apply (default true): also sets the persistent scene's physics capacity (Physics Capacity > Max Bodies) to the recommended one, 1.25 times maxBodiesInRadius for spawns, when the persistent scene is the edited scene in edit mode when the cook starts and when it ends (otherwise a warning says it was not set; an explicit apply: true then fails, writing nothing). One undo step. Saves in flight are waited for, before the cook and before it writes; when the world document was written during the cook (a save listing new cells), the cook starts again from it. Returns staleBefore (cells measured again), maxBodies (the recommended capacity), seconds, and warnings: cells beyond the 20 km worlds are supported within, empty cells.
commands.name: world.cook

apply.description: Also set the persistent scene's physics capacity (default true)

world.description: The world (.stworld): handle or path (asset handle, or path relative to the asset directory)

commands.description: Makes a new world: <path>.stworld and its persistent scene <path>.stscene (the basic3d content, a "World" entity with its WorldComponent; the primary camera streams the cells). Layers default to Terrain, Buildings, Props and Gameplay, each of cellSize meters with a streaming distance of four cells (the first loads before a game starts); give names, or objects {name, cellSize, streamingDistance, enabledByDefault, loadBeforeStart}. open (default true) opens it (failing on unsaved changes unless force; a new history starts, like scene.open; saves in flight are waited for first); without open, one undo step that removes the files. Returns {world, persistentScene, layers}.
commands.name: world.create

cellSize.description: Side of the layers' cells in meters (1-65536, default 64)

force.description: Go on although the edited scene has unsaved changes, discarding them (default false: the command fails instead). Discarded changes are kept as recovery data of the project (scene.recoveryStatus), and the person at the editor is told who discarded them

layers.description: Layer names, or {name, cellSize, streamingDistance, enabledByDefault, loadBeforeStart}

path.description: Path relative to the asset directory without extension, e.g. "Worlds/Island"

commands.description: How the editor edits the open world, for the session: editLayer, the layer new top-level entities go into (a layer's name, or "Persistent" for the persistent scene, the default); visibleLayers, the layers it streams (empty: all); radiusScale, a factor of every layer's streaming distance around the editor camera (0.1-10, default 1). Returns world.status.
commands.name: world.edit

radiusScale.description: Factor of the layers' streaming distances (0.1-10)

commands.description: Describes a world: its name, persistent scene and grid origin, its layers (id, name, cell size and streaming distance in meters, whether they stream by default and load before a game starts, their cells), its cells, and its index (cooked: whether it has one; staleCells: cells changed since it was made, which world.cook measures again; maxBodiesInRadius, persistentBodies and the recommended physics capacity). Distant cells are not loaded at all (no low-detail stand-ins): a game sets fog or far planes to match the layers' streaming distances.
commands.name: world.info

world.description: The world (.stworld): handle or path (asset handle, or path relative to the asset directory)

commands.description: Loads cells of the open world and keeps them (pinned) until unpinned: cells by key ([{layer, x, z}], layer by name or ID) or in a region ({center: [x, y, z], radius} or {min: [x, z], max: [x, z]}, of the given layers or all). pin (default true): false loads them without keeping them (they go when the camera leaves). unpin: cells to let go; unpinAll: let every pinned cell go. wait: answer once the cells are loaded (or failed). Returns {cells: [{layer, x, z, state, entities}]}.
commands.name: world.loadCells

region.description: {center: [x, y, z], radius} or {min: [x, z], max: [x, z]}

unpin.description: Cells to let go: [{layer, x, z}]

wait.description: Answer once the cells are loaded

commands.description: Moves top-level entities of the open world into the cell of a layer at their positions (made when it does not exist yet, written at the next save), or into the persistent scene with layer "Persistent". Their descendants go with them. One undo step. Fails, changing nothing, for a child entity, an unknown layer or a target cell that is not loaded yet (it is loading then: try again once it is in).
commands.name: world.moveEntities

commands.description: Replaces a world's layer list: adds, renames, reorders and retunes layers (streaming distance, enabledByDefault, loadBeforeStart). Layers are matched to the existing ones by id (objects may give it) or name; a rename moves the layer's cell folder (handles kept). Removing a layer that has cells, or changing the cell size of one, is refused unless deleteCells moves those cells to the trash (never cells loaded in the open world: hide the layer first, world.edit visibleLayers). Waits for saves in flight first (they may write the cells it moves). One undo step.
commands.name: world.setLayers

deleteCells.description: Move the cells of removed or re-gridded layers to the trash (default false)

layers.description: Layer names, or {id, name, cellSize, streamingDistance, enabledByDefault, loadBeforeStart}

world.description: The world (.stworld): handle or path (asset handle, or path relative to the asset directory)

commands.description: The world the editor edits (null when the edited scene is no world's persistent scene): its edit layer, visible layers and radius scale (world.edit), the source (the editor camera), its cells' counts (wanted, loading, loaded, unloading, pinned, failed, dirty: changed since saved) and whether the persistent scene is dirty; with cells: true, the cells that are not plain unloaded ones, at most limit (state, entities, dirty, pinned, wanted, error). While playing, playing has the running game's streaming counts.
commands.name: world.status
